## Always do

### Knowledge Priming

- Before non-trivial work, read the README and applicable local instructions. Use an existing architecture contract or index to choose task-relevant sections and skills; when absent, start from the relevant source. A repository-wide audit reads its full inventory.
- When repository evidence and general practice disagree, follow the repository. Say so; do not override it in silence.
- An instruction from the user in the current task overrides this file. A path-scoped instruction overrides it for the files it matches.

### Core Rules

- Make the smallest diff that meets the requirement; build only the requested capability.
- Reuse before building. Establish absence from the code that would use the capability, not documentation or `--help`.
- Fix the root cause and check every call site. Match the edited file's style and names.
- Leave no dead code or debug output. Never swallow errors.
- Keep tests deterministic. A bug fix ships with a regression test. Before writing or changing tests, read `.agents/skills/test-discipline/SKILL.md`.
- Back every claim with evidence: the file, command or passing test.

### Mistake Proofing

Make wrong use impossible or refuse it before damage (poka-yoke).

- Refuse wrong input by name and give the correct command; never return a default or empty success.
- Default to safe behaviour. Require an explicit flag for a mode that can damage shared state.
- Keep each rule in one place and call it from every side.
- Prevent recurrence with a gate or test; a document warning alone does not stop it.

### Data Safety

This application is pointed at real Jira instances, so test fixtures, docs,
screenshots and commit messages are all places customer data can leak in.

- Never commit real customer names, email addresses, domains, Jira URLs, issue
  keys, custom field IDs, API tokens, or exported issue data.
- Use the established placeholders so they stay greppable: `Acme Corp`,
  `example.com`, `customfield_10001`.
- SQL is parameterized, always. No string interpolation into a query, including in
  tests and one-off scripts.
- Validate external API responses before use - a Jira instance can return a shape
  the code does not expect, and an unvalidated field becomes a wrong number on a
  chart.
- `detect-secrets` runs at commit time against `.secrets.baseline`. A new finding
  is resolved by removing the secret, not by re-baselining it.

### Decision Protocol

- Decide from code for small, reversible actions outside the confirmation list.
- Use safe read-only checks to resolve facts first. Ask when missing facts, conflicting sources or uncheckable assumptions change the result. Name the missing fact and useful options.
- With frozen scope, finish started work and demonstrated blockers within scope. Report broader blockers and ask before expanding.
- Record nonblocking adjacent findings in the tracker without implementing them.
- When rules conflict, follow safety and security.
- If an approach fails twice, report the pattern and propose another.

### External Facts

- For third-party interfaces, never rely on memory. Read our adapter, then current vendor documentation; follow `.agents/skills/interface-facts/SKILL.md` for flags, fields, models, prices, limits and versions.
- Before claiming absence or zero, search for the action, not only its name. Run a known-match positive control through the same search. An empty control invalidates the search; a matching control must also increase the examined-item count.
- For a routine observed count, name the checked source or command. Independently derive high-risk quantitative claims and calculations affecting material decisions by two paths sharing no calculation step. Investigate the instrument when they disagree.
- When two causes predict the same result, state both and change the probe until they differ.

### Project Overview

- Purpose: an agile delivery dashboard - burndown and burnup charts, velocity and
  completion forecasting, DORA metrics, flow metrics, and bug analytics - rendered
  from Jira or imported tabular data.
- Stack: Python 3.14+, Dash 4 + Plotly 6 on Waitress, pandas 3 / numpy 2 / scipy for
  the numeric layer, SQLite for persistence, Pydantic for validation.
- Entry point: `app.py`. Production server config in `configuration/server.py`.
- Packages: `data/` business logic and calculations, `visualization/` Plotly figure
  construction, `ui/` component builders and layout, `callbacks/` Dash event wiring,
  `configuration/` settings and in-product help text, `utils/` shared helpers,
  `updater/` self-update, `tests/` pytest suite.
- Architecture references live in `docs/architecture/`; the metrics each chart shows
  are specified in `docs/dashboard_metrics.md`, `docs/dora_metrics.md`,
  `docs/flow_metrics.md`, and indexed by `docs/metrics_index.md`.

### Harness Loop

- If an agent hook reports a missing Lefthook runtime after a clone, run the repository's pinned basicly command with `hooks-build --runtime-only`, then `hooks-check`, and retry. In a basicly source checkout, use `uv run basicly`. Keep the hooks enabled.
- Start with `basicly session start`. Leave a final `[session handover <date>]` note on the root record.
- The tracker ledger is the source of truth for the work.
- The user task request authorizes its scope. Do not request an L-level grant or mandatory token budget.
- Keep verification gates and destructive-action protections enabled. Honor limits the user explicitly sets.
- Use `basicly loop` for non-trivial work. The `harness-loop` skill describes its phases and gates.

### Quality Gate

- Run focused checks while editing and cheap gates first. Run required full verification on the integrated candidate.
- For tracker-only or phase-only changes, rerun affected checks. Reuse passing evidence only when the existing engine establishes equivalent trusted inputs.
- If source or environment inputs change, rerun affected checks. A commit or phase transition alone does not invalidate equivalent evidence.
- If a check fails, fix its cause and rerun affected checks. Keep all required gates enabled.
- In a long run, report the elapsed time, the tokens spent where the host shows them, and the items left.
- Review the diff. Then run the change the way a consumer runs it, and read the output. Passing tests do not prove a working feature.
- After the last edit, run repository checks for what you touched.
- Read the pass or fail summary; truncated output hides failures.
- Report what ran and what did not; expectation is not verification.
- For a claim of complete coverage, name the actual list the code reads.
- Check claims against code before writing plans, designs, READMEs or release notes. Mark unread-code claims as assumptions.
- Before retiring a source system, inventory and account for every original file, including files the import never read.

### Catalog Authoring

- Write catalog sources as YAML, never as a discoverable `.md` file. In a repository that installs basicly, put your sources in `.basicly-local/`, because `basicly install` overwrites `.basicly/core/`.
- Start a source with `basicly catalog new skill` or `basicly catalog new fragment`, and follow the `catalog-authoring` skill. `basicly catalog lint` checks the format. Example source: `.basicly-local/fragments/user/commands/commands.fragment.yaml`; regenerate with `basicly build`.

### Session Completion

- Before you end a session, follow the `session-finish` skill. Leave the repository clean, with no partial edits and no stray files. Report what changed, what you verified and what is still open.
- After a refusal or corrected mistake, resolve its cause within the approved scope. Reuse that diagnosis at handover. Record any further recommendation without expanding the task.

### Python Environment

There is no committed `.venv`, and the git hooks refuse to run without one. Create it
before anything else:

    python -m venv .venv
    .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt

- **Call the venv interpreter directly** rather than activating: `.venv/bin/python`
  (`.venv/Scripts/python.exe` on Windows). Each tool invocation is a fresh shell, so
  an `activate` in one command does not carry into the next - a later bare `python`
  silently runs the system interpreter against the wrong package set.
- Activation, when a human wants it interactively: `source .venv/bin/activate` on
  Linux/macOS/WSL, `source .venv/Scripts/activate` in Git Bash,
  `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` in PowerShell. Keep it in the same command as the work.
- Applies to every Python entry point here, not just the app: `pytest`, `validate.py`,
  `release.py`, `regenerate_changelog.py`, `install_hooks.py`, and any ad-hoc script.
- Development happens on WSL/Linux; Windows is supported and must keep working. Prefer
  cross-platform Python over shell built-ins when there is a choice, and never hardcode
  an absolute path, username, or hostname - they break the other platform silently.
- Write a short script file instead of `python -c "..."` for anything with quoting.
  Inline snippets that survive bash mangle under PowerShell.

### Git Discipline

- Run `git commit` as its own command. Do not chain `git push`, a tag or a tracker update after it, because a refused commit leaves the chain half done.
- The `commit-msg` hooks require a Conventional Commits subject and a trailing record id. The `conventional-commits` skill writes the message, and the `work-tracker` skill claims the record first.
- When a hook refuses a commit, fix the cause it names and commit again. Example subject: `feat(dispatch): bound task context and prioritize integration (basicly-42pn387)`.

### Trunk-Based Workflow

- `main` is the only long-lived branch, and it is the primary protection against
  broken code reaching another developer. Local feature and bugfix branches are fine
  and encouraged for work in progress.
- Integrate by **rebasing onto `main` locally**, then push `main`. There are **no
  remote PRs** - review happens locally before the push. A remote PR is a rare
  exception, not the workflow.
- The pre-commit and pre-push hooks are the real gate. `python validate.py` runs the
  same checks (ruff, djlint, pyright, markdownlint, pytest) in one pass - run it
  before pushing rather than discovering a failure at push time.
- **Never weaken, skip, or bypass a gate to make it pass** - no `--no-verify`, no
  deleting the failing assertion, no loosening a lint rule to silence it. Fix the
  cause. If a gate is genuinely wrong, say so and change it deliberately as its own
  commit.
- The pre-push hook runs the full test suite, so a push takes minutes rather than
  seconds. Let it finish; interrupting it mid-run with another command in the same
  terminal kills pytest partway and the result is meaningless rather than merely
  incomplete.
- Branch deletions and tag pushes skip the quality gate by design.

### Application Release Process

Order matters here: the changelog is written and committed **before** `release.py`
runs, because the release commit and tag are built on top of it.

1. Draft the changelog from history: `.venv/bin/python regenerate_changelog.py
   --preview --json`.
2. Edit `changelog.md` into release notes by hand. Flat bullet lists only, phrased as
   user-visible benefits rather than commit subjects, with major features in bold.
3. Commit the changelog on its own.
4. `.venv/bin/python release.py patch|minor|major` - it bumps the version files,
   regenerates version info, updates the codebase context metrics artifacts, commits,
   tags, and pushes.

- Prefer `release.py` over doing any of those steps by hand; a partially bumped
  version is worse than an unreleased one.
- A release is a push to `main`, so the full gate runs. Do not start one with a red
  suite or an uncommitted working tree.
- Longer form, including packaging specifics: `docs/release_process.md`.

### Platform-Hermetic Tests

- For platform-dependent tests, exercise both platform forms rather than only the host. Read `.agents/skills/test-discipline/SKILL.md` before proceeding.

### Non-Interactive Shell

- Prefer a cross-platform command to shell-specific behaviour.
- Pass a non-interactive flag to a command that can wait for an answer: `cp -f`, `mv -f`, `rm -f`, `-y`, `ssh -o BatchMode=yes`. Some shells alias these commands to interactive mode.
- Never loop over an unquoted variable (`for x in $LIST`). zsh does not split it, so the loop runs once and looks like success. Use an array (`"${arr[@]}"`), an inline list or one batch command, and check that the count changed.
- Before a scripted replace across many sites, state the expected count, and compare it after. A different count is a stop.

### Repo Code Standards

- Size limits, enforced by review rather than by a linter: Python files 500 lines
  and functions 50 lines; JavaScript 400 and 40; HTML 300 lines; CSS 500 lines; a
  single SQL query 50 lines. At 80% of a limit, split into a new module rather than
  appending - but split along a responsibility, never merely by line count. Several
  existing `*_core` / `*_comparison` style splits were made by size alone and are
  harder to follow than the file they came from; do not add more of those.
- Type annotations on every function, except Dash callbacks and test fixtures.
- Naming: `snake_case.py` modules, `PascalCase` classes, `snake_case()` functions,
  `UPPER_CASE` constants. Repository filenames are lowercase (`AGENTS.md`,
  `CLAUDE.md`, `LICENSE` and other tool-mandated names are the exception).
- Logging follows `docs/LOGGING_STANDARDS.md`. Never log credentials, tokens, Jira
  URLs with embedded auth, or customer-identifying values.
- No emoji in code, log output, or comments. Markdown documentation may use them.
- Performance budgets: page load under 2s, chart render under 500ms, interaction
  response under 100ms.
- `python validate.py` runs ruff, djlint, pyright, markdownlint and pytest in one
  pass. Run it before pushing.

### Chart Presentation

A correct number presented misleadingly is as damaging as a wrong number. Charts in
this repo are read by people making commitments, so:

- Projected data must be visually distinguishable from recorded data at a glance -
  dash pattern or opacity, plus a legend entry that says which is which. A reader
  must never mistake a forecast for a fact.
- Confidence bands carry a label saying what they represent. An unlabeled band is
  read as certainty.
- Bar charts start at zero. Truncate an axis only on a line or scatter chart, and
  only where the truncation is visible in the axis labels.
- Charts a user compares side by side share an axis range and a unit. Say the unit
  (story points vs items) in the axis title, and make sure the series actually
  plotted matches it.
- Hover text must show the same value the mark encodes, at a rounding that does not
  contradict the axis.
- Handle the degenerate states deliberately: zero rows, one point, all zeros, and a
  range with no data each need an explicit empty state. A confident flat line drawn
  from no data is a defect.
- The same semantic series keeps the same color across every chart in the app.
  Never encode meaning by color alone, and check contrast in both themes.

### Calculation Integrity

This application's output is numbers people plan against. A wrong number that looks
plausible is the worst defect this repo can ship - worse than a crash, because
nobody investigates it. The numeric layer is held to a higher bar than the rest:

- Never substitute a fallback value for a value you could not compute. Returning
  `0`, `1`, or the previous period's figure when the input was empty, the divisor
  was zero, or the fit did not converge presents a fabricated number as a measured
  one. Return an explicit "not available" and let the caller render it as absent.
- No bare `except` and no `except Exception` around arithmetic or aggregation.
  Catching a computation failure and continuing produces exactly the silent wrong
  answer above. Catch the specific error, or let it raise.
- Guard the degenerate cases explicitly and test them: empty series, a single data
  point, all-zero values, a date range containing no data, and a divisor of zero.
- State the sample size a statistic rests on. A forecast, confidence interval, or
  PERT estimate computed from too few points must carry that fact to the surface
  that renders it, not silently look identical to a well-supported one.
- Do not extrapolate a fit beyond the range its data supports without saying so.
- One metric, one implementation. If a quantity is computed in `data/`, no chart
  prep or callback may recompute it a second way - two implementations of the same
  formula will diverge and both will look right.
- A test that re-implements the formula it is testing proves nothing. Assert against
  known-good expected values worked out independently of the code.
- Changing a formula changes what users already trust. Say so in the changelog
  entry, and say which direction the numbers move.

### Layered Architecture

Each layer has one job, and a dependency may only point downward:

- `callbacks/` - Dash event routing only. Read inputs, call into `data/` or
  `visualization/`, return outputs. No business logic, no calculations, no figure
  construction. A callback that computes something is a bug in the wrong file.
- `data/` - business logic, calculations, external API calls, persistence
  orchestration. Knows nothing about Dash components or Plotly figures.
- `visualization/` - Plotly figure construction. Takes prepared data, returns
  figures. Does not fetch, and does not recompute a metric that `data/` owns.
- `ui/` - component builders and layout assembly. Renders, does not decide.

`ui/` and `visualization/` must not import from `callbacks/`. `data/` must not
import from any of the other three. Where a lazy import inside a function exists to
dodge a cycle, treat it as a defect to be reported, not a pattern to copy.

### Data Architecture

- **Persistence**: one SQLite database at `profiles/burndown.db`, reached through
  `data/persistence/`. Everything under `profiles/` is user data and is gitignored -
  never commit it, never read it into a test fixture, never paste rows into an issue.
- **Schema**: 11 active tables plus `app_state` - `profiles`, `queries`,
  `jira_issues`, `jira_changelog_entries`, `project_statistics`, `project_scope`,
  `metrics_data_points`, `budget_settings`, `budget_revisions`, `task_progress`. A
  legacy `jira_cache` may exist in older databases and is dropped by migrations;
  do not write code that depends on it.
- **Jira access goes through `data/jira_query_manager.py`.** Do not open a second
  client elsewhere - the retry, auth, and field-mapping behavior lives there, and a
  parallel path is how field-mapping bugs become per-call-site bugs.
- **JSON is for export, import, and reports only.** It is never primary storage;
  treat a JSON file as a rendering of the database, not a second source of truth.
- Ad-hoc queries: read-only unless the task is explicitly a write, run through the
  venv interpreter in a short script file, and never print customer-identifying
  columns into terminal output or a generated file that could get committed.

### Dependency Onboarding

Adding a package is explicit onboarding work, and needs confirmation first.

- Runtime dependency: edit `requirements.in`, run `pip-compile requirements.in`,
  then `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
- Development dependency: edit `requirements-dev.in`, run
  `pip-compile requirements-dev.in`, then `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`.
- `requirements.txt` and `requirements-dev.txt` are generated. Never edit them by
  hand; a hand-edit is silently reverted by the next compile.
- State the version constraint's reason in a comment beside it, as the existing
  entries do.
- Vendored browser assets are fetched by `download_vendor_dependencies.py` and
  `download_report_dependencies.py` from `vendor_dependencies.txt` and
  `report_dependencies.txt`; add there, not by committing a bundled file.

### Testing Standards

- Run with pytest; configuration is in `pytest.ini`. Coverage over the layers that
  matter: `pytest --cov=data --cov=visualization --cov=ui`.
- Every test that touches the filesystem uses `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`. A
  test that writes into the repo or a fixed path will pass alone and fail in a
  parallel run.
- Browser-level tests use Playwright. Do not add Selenium.
- A test asserting only "this did not raise" is not coverage. Assert the value.
- Never weaken, skip, or delete a failing test to make a gate pass. A skip needs a
  reason in the skip marker saying what would let it run again.

## Ask first

### Require Explicit Confirmation

These actions need explicit approval. Reuse it only for the same action and scope. Identify that approval. A new phase or agent needs no repeat approval.

- force-push, rewrite history, or discard uncommitted work: `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `git restore`, `git stash`, `git clean`, `rm -rf`;
- read or write a `.env*` file;
- delete files, branches or data outside the task;
- edit CI/CD, deployment, infrastructure, ignore or secrets files;
- add, remove or upgrade a dependency;
- make a network call outside the task.

Tool access does not grant approval. Apply this list even when commands run unblocked. Undo your edit from a prior copy.

## Never do

### Code Is Authoritative

- Never add prose to code: no comment and no docstring. Keep tool directives (example: `noqa`) and licence headers. The `no-comments` hook enforces the ban. For every code edit, read `.agents/skills/no-comments/SKILL.md` for the exceptions, fact placement and hook repair command.

IMPORTANT: never defeat a gate to make it pass. Do not skip or weaken a test, a lint or a type check, and do not bypass a hook (`--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`). Fix the cause.

### Secure Coding

- Never admit unvalidated external input past a trust boundary.
- Never concatenate input into shell syntax or queries; pass arguments and values as parameters.
- Never put secrets in the repository or logs; use environment variables or a secret manager.
- Never expose internal details in returned errors. Log the detail and return a generic message.
- Never commit machine paths, user names or host names. Only the tracker's holder field may record the name chosen with `git config basicly.holder`.
